newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Foreigners take $30 mln in Leumi sale.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners take $30 mln in Leumi sale.

text.p: A public offering in Bank Leumi closed 12 percent above the minimum price, the managing director of the government company charged with privatising Israeli banks said on Wednesday.
"This will bring in an additional 60 million shekels," Meir Jacobson of M.I. Holdings told Reuters.
The closing price was 11.2 shekels for a package of two shares and two free warrants, against a minimum price of 10 shekels. The offering took place on Tuesday.
Leumi shares are trading at 5.18 shekels.

The offering for 15.5 percent of Leumi's share capital was 2.8 times oversubscribed, with 12,000 orders placed. Foreigners received $30 million of the total, less than originally anticipated, because of the higher price.

Jacobson said the sale, the biggest offering ever on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, raised 630 million shekels in cash, including 70 million shekels in shares set aside for bank employees. Underwriters have an option to take up another 1.8 percent of Leumi shares, which would bring in another 100 million shekels.

If exercised, the warrants will raise another 260 million shekels this year and 280 million shekels in 1998. At that point, the government's stake in Leumi, the country's second-biggest bank, will fall to 66 percent.

Finance Minister Dan Meridor said in a statement on Tuesday night that the sale would enable the government to raise three billion shekels from bank privatisations this year, not counting the proceeds from a tender offer now underway for a controlling stake in Bank Hapoalim.
"It should be noted that the completion of the Bank Hapoalim controlling stake could increase the government's proceeds in 1997-1998 by an additional three billion shekels," the Treasury said.
The tender is for 25 to 70 percent of Hapoalim, Israel's largest bank, and is due to be completed by the end of August.
The Leumi offering marks the second big public offering in the government's bank privatisation programme this year. In April, it sold 19 percent of Israel Discount Bank for 620 million shekels.
On Tuesday, the Treasury announced that the Ofer-Wertheim group would exercise an option to take another 25 percent of United Mizrahi Bank for approximately 450 million shekels.
Ofer-Wertheim has a controlling minority stake in Mizrahi, and the Treasury said the sale would reduce the government's stake in Mizrahi to 46 percent.
